title: Build the renderer page
summary: The renderer can use normal HTML, CSS and browser JavaScript.
introduction: The renderer can use normal HTML, CSS and browser JavaScript. Your task: Add a renderer.js click handler using standard DOM methods.
learningObjectives: Add a renderer.js click handler using standard DOM methods.
Explain the example for build the renderer page

blocks.text: The renderer can use normal HTML, CSS and browser JavaScript. It does not need Node access to show a button or change words.

Use a local Electron project with electron installed as a dev dependency and main.cjs as its main file. Run with npx electron . after creating package.json and index.html. These APIs do not run in a web-page playground.

items: The local HTML supplies the screen and references a separate renderer script.
The script can use normal browser events without enabling Node access in the page.

blocks.text: Save as index.html and create renderer.js for the button behaviour. Electron displays it as a normal local page.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Keep desktop-only operations out of ordinary renderer code. Use an approved bridge when a real desktop capability is needed.
